reports.title: Atour Lifestyle Holdings Limited Reports Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: For the full year of 2026, the Company currently expects total net revenues to increase by 33% to 35% compared with the full year of 2025.
This outlook is based on current market conditions and the Company’s preliminary estimates, which are subject to changes.

desk.headline: Revenue up 30.5% to RMB3.43bn on 61% retail growth; GAAP profit down 5.5% on share pay; FY26 revenue growth outlook raised to 33–35%

numbers.eps_basis: diluted GAAP per ordinary share (RMB3.30 per ADS)

results: Net revenue rose 30.5% to RMB3.43bn (US$511m); retail (mainly sleep products) jumped 61% to RMB1.36bn and franchised-managed hotels grew 20%.
Share-based pay rose to RMB167m from RMB13m, so GAAP net income fell 5.5% to RMB448m; excluding it, profit rose 26% to RMB615m.
Hotel trading was flat: RevPAR RMB373 vs RMB371 a year ago, with occupancy 79.7% and same-hotel RevPAR down about 4%.
The network grew to 2,288 hotels (128 opened in the quarter) with 778 in the pipeline.
A second 2026 dividend of US$0.51 per ADS (about US$69m) was declared, payable around 9 Dec; cash and restricted cash stood at RMB2.8bn.

guidance.summary: Atour now expects 2026 net revenue to grow 33–35%, up from about 30% given with Q2 results. On the call it also lifted retail growth to 50–55% (from 40%) and kept its target of about 480 hotel openings.

points: Management raised retail growth guidance for a third time this year after strong sales of core and new product lines.
The adjusted profit margin dipped as the mix shifted toward retail and the company kept investing in staff.
No numbers were given for Q4 RevPAR or for 2027; holiday travel and a recovery in business trips were cited as support.
Dividends and buybacks so far in 2026 exceed US$260m, more than all of 2025 net income; the aim is to return about 100% of prior-year profit.
call.source: CEO comments in the results release; call coverage: Earnings Whispers call summary and analysis, 10 Nov 2026

watch: Whether share-based pay stays high and keeps weighing on GAAP profit.
Same-hotel RevPAR, which fell about 4% this quarter, and the shrinking pipeline (778 from 811).
Retail growth against the new 50–55% target in Q4, including the Singles' Day shopping season.
